questions.q: Why does the chapter revisit professional help after the retreat?
options: Because every retreat causes problems
Because three days of quiet often make visible what months of noise had covered
Because pastors require it
Because the rule of life always fails
questions.explanation: Before the retreat the question was whether you were safe to go. Now the question is what the retreat showed you. This chapter is not a verdict; it is a map.

questions.q: Which post-retreat sign does the chapter say is a reason to seek help?
options: Feeling flat for the first two days home
A dip that has lasted most days for two weeks or more, or is deepening rather than easing
Missing the rhythm once
Wanting another retreat
questions.explanation: Do not wait two weeks if symptoms are severe, rapidly worsening, preventing ordinary functioning, or include thoughts of suicide or self-harm. Seek help now.

questions.q: According to the 'Who does what' table, who is the appropriate help for persistent low mood, panic, or trauma symptoms affecting daily functioning?
options: A pastor only
A doctor or qualified mental-health professional
A small group
A retreat centre
questions.explanation: Most serious difficulties need more than one kind of help, and a pastor is often one part. The mistake is going only to a pastor for something a pastor is not trained to treat.

questions.q: What is the chapter's answer to 'medication would be a spiritual defeat'?
options: Medication is always the answer
Medication is a medical treatment, not a verdict on your faith; discuss it with a qualified prescriber and do not change it because of a retreat experience
Christians should never take medication
Only pastors may decide
questions.explanation: Luke was a physician; Paul told Timothy to take a remedy. Prayer, pastoral support, medicine and therapy can work together.

questions.q: What should a pastor or leader do about getting help?
options: Receive counselling from a member of their own congregation
Find help outside their own church, such as a denominational provision, supervisor, or counsellor with clergy experience
Keep it entirely secret from everyone
Wait until they are no longer in ministry
questions.explanation: A dual relationship is unfair to both people. Keep clinical details private and follow safeguarding and employment requirements.

questions.q: How does the chapter describe a crisis of faith after a retreat?
options: As a mental-health condition
As proof the retreat was a mistake
As not a mental-health condition and not necessarily a sign anything is wrong; often what happens when a faith carried by activity stops moving
As something to hide from everyone
questions.explanation: Do not carry it alone, and do not carry it to someone who will panic. Faith allowed to ask honest questions can become more mature, though the process is slow.

reflection: Did any of the post-retreat signs describe you? Which?
Using the table, who is the right first call for what you are carrying? Write the kind of help, not yet the name.
Which of the objections has been holding you back, if any? Write the answer to it in your own words.
